title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 155 (Effect of mixture, with bailor’s consent, of his goods with bailee’s)

content.overview: Section 155 provides that if the bailee, with the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods, the bailor and the bailee shall have an interest, in proportion to their respective shares, in the mixture thus produced.
content.glance: Where the bailee mixes the bailor’s goods with his own with the bailor’s consent, both have a proportionate interest in the resulting mixture.
content.study: If the bailee, with the consent of the bailor, mixes the goods of the bailor with his own goods, the bailor and the bailee shall have an interest, in proportion to their respective shares, in the mixture thus produced. Current-law framing: consent converts the mixture into a co-owned mass in proportion to the respective contributions.

examples.title: Consented mixture
examples.body: Bailor consents to mixing his grain with the bailee’s grain. Both have a proportionate interest in the resulting mixture under Section 155.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 155 provides that where the bailee mixes the bailor’s goods with his own with the bailor’s consent, the bailor and the bailee shall have an interest, in proportion to their respective shares, in the mixture thus produced. This is the consensual counterpart to the non-consensual rules in Sections 156 and 157.
examples: Consented mixing of grain creates proportionate co-ownership of the mixture.
distinctions: Section 155 (with consent) creates proportionate interests; Sections 156–157 address non-consensual mixtures (separable or inseparable).
keyTakeaways: Consented mixture creates proportionate interests in the resulting mixture.
